topic: Matrix Multiplication: The Art of Composition
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Matrix as a Movement
lecture_lines: Meet our Geometry Robot, starting at coordinate one zero.
Matrix A acts as a rule for rotating space.
As the grid transforms, the basis vectors change position.
Our Robot follows this motion, rotating to zero one.
Matrix columns track exactly where those basis vectors land.
animations: Create a coordinate grid (#555555) with the robot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] (#00FF00) at position (1, 0).
Fade in the rotation Matrix A [[0, -1], [1, 0]] in yellow (#FFFF00) on the screen.
Animate the grid transforming; show basis vector i (#FF0000) moving to (0, 1) and basis vector j (#0000FF) moving to (-1, 0).
The robot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] (#00FF00) follows the grid transformation, landing at the coordinate (0, 1).
Highlight the columns of Matrix A in yellow (#FFFF00) to show they represent the transformed basis vectors.

sections.title: The Sequential Challenge
lecture_lines: Let's restart our Robot at its original position.
First, Matrix A rotates the Robot ninety degrees.
Now, we introduce Matrix B to add a shear.
Matrix B shifts the Robot to its final destination.
We can track the full path of this journey.
animations: Show the Robot (#00FF00) at its starting position (1, 0) on a fresh grid (#555555).
Apply Matrix A (Rotation) and pause; the Robot moves to (0, 1) with an intermediate label.
Fade in Matrix B [[1, 1], [0, 1]] (Shear) in cyan (#00FFFF) next to Matrix A.
Apply Matrix B to the already transformed grid; the Robot moves from (0, 1) to (1, 1).
Draw a dashed line path showing the trajectory from start to middle to end.

sections.title: Defining the 'Shortcut' (The Product)
lecture_lines: We want to skip the intermediate movement step.
Matrix C is the product of applying B after A.
This Master Matrix teleports the Robot in one leap.
animations: Show the Robot at start (1, 0) and final end (1, 1) positions simultaneously on the grid.
Display the multiplication BA = C, where C is [[0, -1], [1, 1]] in magenta (#FF00FF).
Animate the Robot teleporting directly from (1, 0) to (1, 1) using the transformation Matrix C.

sections.title: The Right-to-Left Rule
lecture_lines: In notation, the first action sits on the right.
Like a conveyor belt, vectors enter from the right.
Matrix A acts first, then Matrix B follows.
animations: Write (BA)v on screen, highlighting 'A' then 'B' sequentially from right to left.
Visualize a conveyor belt: Vector 'v' enters machine A, then the output enters machine B.
Label the sequence as 'Right-to-Left' composition using arrows.

sections.title: Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)
lecture_lines: In matrix math, the order of actions matters.
Rotating then shearing leads to a specific destination.
Shearing then rotating ends in a completely different spot.
Since BA and AB differ, multiplication is non-commutative.
Visualizing these paths proves order is everything.
animations: Split the screen; display 'B then A' on the left and 'A then B' on the right.

On the left, Robot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] rotates then shears; on the right, Robot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] shears then rotates.
Show both Robots [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] landing in different final positions on their respective grids.
Draw a bright red (#FF0000) 'X' mark at the two different destinations for contrast.
Display the large text 'BA!= AB' in the center to emphasize non-commutativity.

sections.title: Summary: The DNA of Transformation
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication is just the composition of movements.
One matrix captures a sequence of complex transformations.
Think of products as instructions for a final destination.
animations: Animate a sequence of three matrices multiplying together into a single 'Master Matrix'.
Show a complex geometric pattern transforming in one step using this Master Matrix.
End with the text 'Matrix multiplication is composition' in bright white (#FFFFFF).
